title: Wings agree a business arrangement | 1971
content:
With the bulk of the Wild Life album recorded, the future members of Wings returned to Scotland to discuss their future.

They undertook a number of rehearsal sessions at the McCartneys’ Rude Studio, and began to discuss how a band model might look.

Paul McCartney was keen to be part of another band, rather than a solo artist, but acknowledged that he would be the main draw to audiences.

Paul said, ‘You guys are gonna be part owners of this band.’ Now, anytime you get a chance to be in a band with Paul McCartney and be a shareholder of the situation, I don’t think money’s gonna be an object.
Denny Seiwell, 6 June 2016
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair

The solution outlined by McCartney was to pay Denny Laine and Denny Seiwell £70 each per week. There were no contracts signed, but all parties were happy with the arrangement – for the time being.

On 9 August, following a rehearsal and final discussions, an impromptu party was held outside Rude Studios at High Park Farm. The musicians raised tumblers and mugs filled with scotch and Coke, as photographed by Monique Seiwell.
